sentences.text: TAMMY: You know when you went to the Shetland Islands last year, Paul? Did you go by ferry or did you fly?
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 保罗，你知道去年你去设得兰群岛的时候吗？你是坐渡轮去的，还是坐飞机去的？

sentences.text: PAUL: We went by ferry, Tammy. I prefer driving to flying - the journey feels like part of the holiday.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 我们坐的是渡轮，塔米。比起坐飞机，我更喜欢自己开车——旅途本身就像是假期的一部分。

sentences.text: TAMMY: Mmm. Which ferry company did you use?
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 嗯。你们用的是哪家渡轮公司？

sentences.text: PAUL: There's only one - it's called Northern Ferries. The ferries all leave from Aberdeen.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 只有一家，叫北方渡轮公司（Northern Ferries）。所有渡轮都从阿伯丁出发。

sentences.text: TAMMY: How frequent are they?
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 渡轮班次有多频繁？

sentences.text: PAUL: The service is pretty limited - there's only one ferry leaving every evening in summer anyway, seven days a week - I'm not sure about the winter months.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 这项服务相当有限——夏天每周七天，每天只有一班晚间渡轮；至于冬季班次，我就不清楚了。

sentences.text: TAMMY: They may only run on four or five days then.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 那么冬季可能一周只运行四到五天。

sentences.text: PAUL: OK. So it's an overnight trip. I quite like that idea. Leaving at night and waking up as you arrive on the island. Can you remember how much you paid for your tickets?
sentences.zh: PAUL: 好的。所以这是一趟过夜行程。我很喜欢这个想法：晚上出发，抵达岛屿时正好醒来。你还记得你们船票花了多少钱吗？

sentences.text: TAMMY: They were really cheap and four people and a car worked out at just under £250.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 票价非常便宜，四个人加一辆车总共不到250英镑。

sentences.text: PAUL: Really? I was expecting it to be more like £400 during the peak season.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 真的吗？我原本以为旺季期间要接近400英镑呢。

sentences.text: TAMMY: So was I. It's great value. It's a good idea to book in advance because I think they get booked up quite quickly - especially during the school holidays.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 我也是这么想的。性价比很高。提前预订是个好主意，因为我觉得船票很快就会售罄——尤其是学校放假期间。

sentences.text: PAUL: Yes, I suppose so. I'm just not 100% sure of our plans yet. What if I had to cancel?
sentences.zh: PAUL: 是啊，我想也是。不过我们目前还没完全确定行程。万一我需要取消怎么办？

sentences.text: TAMMY: That could be a problem. I don't think it's their policy to give refunds - just a voucher - which you can use at a later date. But you have to cancel a month in advance to get that.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 那可能会是个问题。据我所知，他们并不提供退款，只发代金券——日后可使用。但必须提前一个月取消才能拿到代金券。

sentences.text: PAUL: Right. Well we need to make up our minds quickly then.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 明白了。那我们得尽快做决定了。

sentences.text: TAMMY: You'd want to book a cabin too. We booked too late to get a cabin with a window. They're more expensive but much nicer than the inner cabins. You don't have to book a cabin at all but I think it's worth paying for. They also have luxury cabins, which are only for two people and have a TV - but I wouldn't bother with those.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 你们还得预订客舱。我们订得太晚，没能订到带窗户的客舱。这类客舱价格更高，但比内舱舒适得多。虽然不订客舱也可以，但我认为值得多花点钱。他们还有豪华客舱，仅限两人入住，并配有电视——不过我觉得没必要选那种。

sentences.text: PAUL: No, I agree.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 对，我也这么认为。

sentences.text: TAMMY: The only other thing I can think of is to make sure you bring snacks for the kids.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 我能想到的另一件事，就是务必给孩子们带上零食。

sentences.text: PAUL: The selection on board is quite limited and not that healthy either.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 船上的食品选择很有限，而且也不太健康。

sentences.text: TAMMY: Mmm. What about wifi on board? Is that any good?
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 嗯。船上提供Wi-Fi吗？信号怎么样？

sentences.text: PAUL: Not really. So it's best to bring some books for them.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 实际上不太好。所以最好给他们带几本书。

sentences.text: TAMMY: OK. We may need to bring the dog if I can't get anyone to look after him.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 好的。如果我找不到人照看狗狗，我们可能得把它带上。

sentences.text: PAUL: We brought ours and it was fine. The kennels on board are OK - they're quite big - you just need to provide a blanket.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 我们带了自家的狗，一切都很顺利。船上的犬舍条件不错——空间相当宽敞——你只需自备一条毯子即可。

sentences.text: TAMMY: Uhuh. Sounds good.
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 嗯嗯，听起来不错。

sentences.text: PAUL: It was all very easy really - and it was quite an adventure for the kids. They loved being on the sea at night and in the morning keeping a lookout for dolphins - we saw loads.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 整个过程其实非常轻松，对孩子们来说还是一次相当有趣的冒险。他们特别喜欢夜间航行在海上，以及清晨守候观望海豚——我们看到了好多只。

sentences.text: TAMMY: OS Oh, the kids would love that!
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 哦，孩子们一定会喜欢这个！

sentences.text: PAUL: One other thing. We arrived in Aberdeen hours before the ferry was due to leave so we decided to go somewhere else rather than hang around at the port for so long.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 还有一件事：我们抵达阿伯丁的时间比渡轮预定出发时间早了好几个小时，于是决定去别处逛逛，而不是在港口长时间干等。

sentences.text: TAMMY: Where did you go?
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 你们去了哪儿？

sentences.text: PAUL: Drum Castle.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 德鲁姆城堡（Drum Castle）。

sentences.text: TAMMY: I've never heard of it. Is that spelt like the instrument?
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 我从来没听说过这个地方。拼写跟乐器‘鼓’（drum）一样吗？

sentences.text: PAUL: Yeah. It's really worth visiting. It's got an impressive tower and beautiful gardens and ancient woodland.
sentences.zh: PAUL: 是的。它非常值得一游，拥有一座令人印象深刻的塔楼、美丽的花园以及古老的林地。

sentences.text: TAMMY: Sounds lovely. Does it have a restaurant?
sentences.zh: TAMMY: 听起来真棒。那里有餐厅吗？

sentences.text: It's only got a coffee shop - no restaurant. We looked up restaurants in the area and found an Italian one in a village nearby. I can check the name of it for you if you're interested.
sentences.zh: 那里只有一家咖啡馆，没有餐厅。我们查了周边地区的餐厅，发现附近一个村庄里有家意大利餐厅。如果你感兴趣，我可以帮你确认一下它的名字。

sentences.text: Oh thanks Paul that would be....
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢保罗，那太好了……

sentences.text: Good evening everyone. My name's Jon and I run Veg Out, a street food business selling vegan food. Since 2012 I've been travelling all around the country cooking vegan food in my converted van and selling it at all kinds of outdoor events. I'm here to give you some advice based on my experience.
sentences.zh: 晚上好，各位。我叫乔恩，经营着一家名为“素食出街”的街头食品生意，专门售卖纯素食食品。自2012年起，我便开着改装后的厢式货车走遍全国，在各类户外活动中现场烹饪并售卖纯素食。

sentences.text: The good news is that there's never been a better time to start your own street food business. Street food continues to grow in popularity. I think there are a couple of reasons for this. The first is that street food is a reaction against fast food. Street food ranges from high quality burgers to vegan curries and everything in between. But while fast food is cheap and easy to find, it's not particularly good for you. It's also the same everywhere.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，现在开启自己的街头食品生意比以往任何时候都更合适。街头食品持续升温、广受欢迎。我认为原因有二：其一，街头食品是对快餐文化的一种反拨；街头食品种类繁多，从高品质汉堡到纯素咖喱，应有尽有。但快餐虽价格低廉、随处可得，却并不健康，且千篇一律。

sentences.text: What you get with street food on the other hand is something different. People like the idea of trying something they can't get anywhere else. They also like seeing food prepared in front of them and which hasn't come straight out of a freezer.
sentences.zh: 而街头食品则恰恰相反——它独具特色。人们乐于尝试别处吃不到的美食；也喜欢亲眼看着食物现场制作，而非直接从冰柜中取出。

sentences.text: You need to think about the best place to sell your street food. People always think music festivals are an obvious place to start but the cost of renting a space can be huge. And there's always a lot of competition. Food markets. on the other hand. are great because customers are always really interested in food and give great feedback. And if you can get a spot in your local park - fantastic. Usually very relaxed but with lots of customers passing by. Once you get established you'll start getting asked to do parties - which can be really challenging but lots of fun. Having street food at weddings has become quite fashionable too - but you need to really know what you're doing as everything needs to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 你需要认真考虑最适合售卖街头食品的地点。人们总以为音乐节是显而易见的起点，但租用摊位的费用可能极其高昂，而且竞争向来激烈。相比之下，美食市集却是极佳选择——顾客始终对美食抱有浓厚兴趣，并乐于提供宝贵反馈。若能在本地公园觅得一席之地，那就再好不过了：氛围通常轻松惬意，且人流量大。一旦站稳脚跟，你便会陆续接到派对邀约——这虽颇具挑战性，却也充满乐趣。如今在婚礼上提供街头食品也渐成风尚，但你必须对此驾轻就熟，因为一切细节都须臻于完美。

sentences.text: Setting up a street food business costs a lot less than opening a restaurant or café but you'll 011/12 011/12 013/14 013/14 have to buy some basic equipment. I'd try to get things like hobs and fridges second hand O 15 if you can. You can replace them with better quality stuff if your business takes off. Renting is another option but you'll end up spending more money rather than saving it.
sentences.zh: 开设街头食品生意所需投入远低于开餐厅或咖啡馆，但仍需购置一些基础设备。我建议尽可能二手采购炉灶、冰箱等设备；若生意蒸蒸日上，再逐步更换为更高品质的装备。租赁也是一种选择，但最终往往花费更多，而非节省开支。

sentences.text: You've probably got a good idea about the food you're planning to sell. I expect you've done some research to find out if anyone else is selling a similar product. And you'll have thought about any possible allergies to nuts or eggs etc. But there's one thing people don't always think about and that's how you're going to serve it. On a plate? In a bag? Will you provide a fork? Will it all be easily recyclable or reusable? It's got to be easy to eat and look attractive or customers won't come back.
sentences.zh: 你大概已对自己计划售卖的食品有了清晰构想。想必你也做过调研，确认是否已有他人销售同类产品；也考虑过坚果、鸡蛋等常见过敏原问题。但有一件事常被忽略——即食品的呈现方式：盛于盘中？装入纸袋？是否提供叉子？所有包装是否易于回收或重复使用？食品必须便于食用且外观诱人，否则顾客不会回头。

sentences.text: Once you get started, you should be prepared for things to go wrong. Every business faces problems and here are a few examples from street food businesses that I know.
sentences.zh: 一旦起步，你就要做好应对各种突发状况的心理准备。每家生意都会遭遇难题，以下是我所知几家街头食品商家的真实案例。

sentences.text: My friends who run Thai Basil started by juggling their street food business with their day jobs in a restaurant. Their work-life balance was non-existent as they were working til midnight in O 17 the restaurant all week and then took their food truck to markets on their days off.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友经营‘泰香罗勒’，起初一边在餐厅从事全职工作，一边兼顾街头食品生意。他们完全丧失了工作与生活的平衡——整周在餐厅工作至午夜，仅靠休息日将餐车开赴市集。

sentences.text: The owners of Basque found it was hard to make a profit because the price of fish - O 18 essential for some of their dishes - was so high. And it was hard to charge customers a lot more for those dishes. So they had to stop focussing on fish dishes and include more vegetarian food.
sentences.zh: ‘巴斯克’的经营者发现盈利艰难，因其部分招牌菜必备的鱼类成本极高；而向顾客大幅提价又难以实现。最终他们不得不减少鱼类菜品比重，转而增加素食选项。

sentences.text: The owners of Lou's kitchen were making salads to order from their van and some of their O 19 dishes were quite complicated. At one of their first events they ended up with people standing in a long queue for more than 15 minutes - and many of them lost patience. So make sure whatever you offer can be served quickly and efficiently.
sentences.zh: ‘露厨房’的经营者在厢式货车内按单制作沙拉，部分菜品工序相当复杂。在首次活动时，顾客排起长队等候逾15分钟，许多人失去耐心、愤然离去。因此，请务必确保所售食品能快速高效地完成出品。

sentences.text: The owners of Chip Chop had found a perfect venue near a beach where there weren't any other street food trucks. But what they hadn't realised was that they'd need a special licence - which individual businesses don't need at markets or festivals. It was a complicated process and in the end they gave up.
sentences.zh: ‘薯条切切’的经营者在一处临近海滩的理想场地落脚，周边并无其他街头餐车。但他们未曾意识到，该地点需申领特殊执照——而此类执照在市集或音乐节等场合并非个体商户必需。申办流程极为繁琐，最终他们只得放弃。

sentences.text: So I hope that's given you a flavour of....
sentences.zh: 希望以上分享能让大家对……有所了解。

sentences.text: MADDY: Shall we go through our research for our sustainable fashion project?
sentences.zh: MADDY: 我们来梳理一下可持续时尚项目的调研内容吧？

sentences.text: RYAN: Good idea. I think I've done enough reading now.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 好主意。我觉得我现在已经阅读得差不多了。

sentences.text: MADDY: Me too. I've learnt such a lot about what sustainability actually means.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 我也是。我对‘可持续性’的实际含义了解了很多。

sentences.text: RYAN: Mmm, same for me with ethical fashion. I didn't really appreciate the difference between that and sustainable fashion before doing this research.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 嗯，我对‘道德时尚’也有了类似的认识。在开展这项调研之前，我其实并不太清楚它与可持续时尚之间的区别。

sentences.text: MADDY: I know - most people use these terms interchangeably - but in fact the difference is quite distinct when you think about it. Sustainable relates to the environment and ethical relates more to the way workers or animals are treated.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 我知道——大多数人都是混用这些术语的——但仔细思考后，两者的区别其实相当明确：‘可持续’关乎环境，而‘道德’则更多涉及对工人或动物的对待方式。

sentences.text: RYAN: I totally understand why people get confused, though. There are so many other terms used - like 'eco-friendly', which is actually quite meaningless.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 不过，我完全理解人们为何会混淆。还有太多其他术语被使用——比如‘环保型’（eco-friendly），这个词实际上意义非常模糊。

sentences.text: MADDY: And the way companies use these terms when describing their products doesn't help. They're often deliberately vague. I think. and don't provide enough information about how their products are made.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 而且企业描述自家产品时使用这些术语的方式也无助于厘清概念。它们往往刻意含糊其辞，我认为，也未能充分说明产品是如何生产的。

sentences.text: RYAN: Yes.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 是的。

sentences.text: MADDY: It was interesting to read about the debates surrounding wool production and how ethical and sustainable that is. It's generally considered to be sustainable because it's a natural product.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 阅读有关羊毛生产及其道德性与可持续性的相关争论很有意思。羊毛通常被认为具有可持续性，因为它是天然产物。

sentences.text: RYAN: And it also lasts a long time and can be recycled. All very positive. But I wasn't convinced by the argument that wool production is sustainable because it doesn't use many chemicals - what about all the fungicides and insecticides used in sheep farming?
sentences.zh: RYAN: 而且它耐用性强，还可回收利用，这些都是非常积极的特点。但我并不认同‘羊毛生产是可持续的，因为它使用化学品很少’这一论点——那么绵羊养殖中使用的大量杀菌剂和杀虫剂又该怎么算呢？

sentences.text: MADDY: Good point. And I couldn't find any evidence for the claim about sheep farming being better for the environment than cattle farming.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 说得很好。而且我也找不到任何证据支持‘绵羊养殖比牛养殖对环境更友好’这一说法。

sentences.text: RYAN: No - they're both really bad. I read different reports about how unethical it is to even shear sheep. Some people say it's cruel but as long as the sheep are kept in good condition I can't see anything wrong with it.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 没错——两者其实都对环境极为不利。我还读到一些报告，讨论给绵羊剪毛本身是否不道德。有人认为这是残忍行为，但只要绵羊处于良好饲养状态，我就看不出其中有什么问题。

sentences.text: MADDY: Me neither.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 我也这么认为。

sentences.text: RYAN: Shall we talk about some of the semi-synthetic new fabrics now?
sentences.zh: RYAN: 接下来我们谈谈一些新型半合成面料吧？

sentences.text: MADDY: OK, let's do that.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 好的，那就开始吧。

sentences.text: RYAN: Let's start with Lyocell, I've been reading about that.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 我们先从莱赛尔（Lyocell）说起，我最近一直在研究这种材料。

sentences.text: MADDY: Yeah, that's the one produced from the pulp of eucalyptus trees, isn't it?
sentences.zh: MADDY: 对，就是那种由桉树浆制成的面料，对吧？

sentences.text: RYAN: Yes, and what happens with that is really impressive. Over 99% of dissolving agents used in the manufacturing process are used again.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 没错，而且它的生产工艺确实令人印象深刻：制造过程中所用溶解剂的99%以上都能被循环再利用。

sentences.text: MADDY: Yeah. Now, there are a few semi-synthetic fabrics that I'd never heard of. Like Cupro, for example.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 是的。现在有一些半合成面料我以前听都没听说过，比如铜氨纤维（Cupro）。

sentences.text: RYAN: Made from byproducts of the cotton industry to create a kind of vegan silk.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 它是由棉产业的副产品制成的，可作为一种纯素丝绸。

sentences.text: MADDY: But I'm not sure how sustainable this really is as there are so many reports of pollution caused by the manufacturing process.
sentences.zh: MADEY: 但我并不确定这实际上是否可持续，因为有很多报告指出其制造过程会造成污染。

sentences.text: RYAN: Mmm. It doesn't compare favourably with all the other sustainable fabrics we've looked at, no.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 嗯。与其他我们考察过的可持续面料相比，它确实不占优势。

sentences.text: MADDY: Bamboo is one fabric we're all familiar with. But I didn't know that it was only organic bamboo that's truly sustainable.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 竹纤维是一种我们都熟悉的面料。但以前我并不知道，只有有机竹纤维才是真正可持续的。

sentences.text: RYAN: Me neither. Apparently. the manufacturing process for a significant proportion of bamboo is chemically quite intensive - which obviously can be quite damaging.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 我也不知道。显然，目前大部分竹纤维的制造过程在化学处理方面强度很高——这显然可能造成相当严重的损害。

sentences.text: MADDY: EcoVero is an example of a semi-synthetic fabric which is becoming really popular.
sentences.zh: MADDY: EcoVero 是一种半合成面料的范例，正变得越来越受欢迎。

sentences.text: RYAN: Probably because manufacturing causes 50 percent fewer emissions and takes up half as much energy as conventional fabrics. That saves production costs as well as being better for the environment.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 这可能是因为其制造过程产生的排放量比传统面料减少50%，且能耗仅为传统面料的一半。这不仅有利于环境，还能节省生产成本。

sentences.text: MADDY: That's true. I think demand for cork will continue to grow. It works really well in vegan shoes and bags.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 没错。我认为软木的需求将持续增长。它在纯素鞋类和包袋中表现非常出色。

sentences.text: RYAN: Mmm and it's the only fabric that's fundamentally sustainable - the cork trees it comes from are renewable and the product itself is both recyclable and biodegradable - which is unique.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 嗯，而且它是唯一一种本质上就具备可持续性的面料——其原料软木树本身可再生，而软木产品本身既可回收又可生物降解——这一点十分独特。

sentences.text: MADDY: And the harvesting process is actually good for the trees. There are no downsides to using this source at all.
sentences.zh: MADDY: 而且采收过程实际上对树木有益。使用这种原料完全没有任何缺点。

sentences.text: RYAN: Hemp is another really good sustainable fabric from a natural source.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 麻纤维是另一种来自天然来源的极佳可持续面料。

sentences.text: MADDY: Yes. Did you know that clothes made from hemp protect the wearer from the sun and it's also antibacterial?
sentences.zh: MADDY: 是的。你知道用大麻纤维制成的衣物能保护穿着者免受阳光伤害，同时还具有抗菌性能吗？

sentences.text: RYAN: No. I didn't. But I did read that it's quite hard to grow, so perhaps that"s why it's not as common as you'd think.
sentences.zh: RYAN: 不知道。但我确实读到过，大麻种植难度较大，这或许就是它不像人们预想中那么普及的原因。

sentences.text: I'm sure that'll change.
sentences.zh: 我确信这种情况将会改变。

sentences.text: Today I'm going to talk about invasive species. Let me start by saying what an invasive species is and what it's not. Invasive species are any animal or plant that is introduced into an environment by humans, and which is then harmful to that environment. It's important to be clear that not all introduced species are invasive. Many introduced - or non-native - species thrive in new areas without posing any threat.
sentences.zh: 今天我要讲的是入侵物种。首先，让我说明什么是入侵物种，以及什么不是入侵物种。入侵物种是指由人类引入某一环境的任何动物或植物，并对该环境造成危害。需要明确的是，并非所有被引入的物种都是入侵物种。许多被引入（即非本地）的物种在新环境中茁壮成长，却并未构成任何威胁。

sentences.text: In some cases, invasive species have changed the natural world beyond recognition, so let's look at the different ways they can be problematic. First of all, invasive species may eat native species, or sometimes they may bring a disease with them, which native species have never faced before and therefore have no defences against. Often the invasive species breed very quickly - which further adds to the problem of native species losing their sources of food. Species invasions are one of the biggest causes of damage in an ecosystem, actually putting its survival at risk.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，入侵物种已彻底改变了自然世界，使其面目全非，因此我们来了解一下它们可能造成问题的不同方式。首先，入侵物种可能会捕食本地物种；有时它们还会携带来自原生地的疾病，而这些疾病是本地物种从未遭遇过的，因而毫无防御能力。通常，入侵物种繁殖速度极快——这进一步加剧了本地物种食物来源丧失的问题。物种入侵是生态系统遭受破坏的最主要原因之一，实际上已危及生态系统的存续。

sentences.text: So, how do invasive species spread? Without a doubt, the biggest cause is human activity.
sentences.zh: 那么，入侵物种是如何扩散的呢？毫无疑问，最主要的原因是人类活动。

sentences.text: This could be intentional, or it could be accidental, such as when people who've been on holiday in another country come back with, say, the seeds of plants on their clothes or shoes. Plants and animals, especially insects, arrive in or on the cargo of ships, and then escape into their new 'home'. But sometimes humans deliberately move animals and plants around the world, for example to use them to control pests on farms, or to be pets. This can go very wrong if those animals and plants move into wild settings and start breeding or begin growing in ways that weren't predicted.
sentences.zh: 这种扩散可能是有意为之，也可能是无意之举；例如，人们从其他国家度假归来时，衣服或鞋上可能沾有植物种子。植物和动物——尤其是昆虫——会随船舶货物抵达新地区，随后逃逸到其新的‘家园’中。但有时人类会刻意将动植物运往世界各地，例如为控制农场害虫，或作为宠物饲养。倘若这些动植物进入野外环境并开始繁殖，或以始料未及的方式生长，就可能造成严重后果。

sentences.text: Let's now look at an example of an invasive species here in Australia: Rhinella marina is a species of toad that was deliberately introduced from Hawaii in 1935 as a form of biological control. It was hoped that the toads would eat the grey-backed beetles responsible for destroying crops of sugar on many of the plantations. At first, just a handful of toads were released by scientists into Queensland, but this number soon grew as other states followed suit. Within two years, 62, young toads had been released into the wild. The toads did nothing to protect the plantations, but they did reproduce rapidly and could soon be found all over the northern half of the country. The toads are poisonous at every stage of their life cycle, and anything that eats them will die.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们来看一个澳大利亚境内的入侵物种实例：海蟾蜍（Rhinella marina）是一种于1935年从夏威夷有意引进的蟾蜍，目的是进行生物防治。当时人们希望这种蟾蜍能捕食灰背甲虫——这种甲虫正严重破坏许多甘蔗种植园的作物。起初，科学家仅在昆士兰州野外释放了少量蟾蜍，但很快其他州纷纷效仿。两年之内，已有62只幼年蟾蜍被放归野外。这些蟾蜍对保护甘蔗种植园毫无作用，却迅速繁殖，很快便遍布全国北部地区。海蟾蜍在其整个生命周期中均具毒性，任何捕食它们的动物都会死亡。

sentences.text: My second example regarding invasive species is the United Kingdom. Actually, there are more than three-thousand invasive species there, including some that are extremely common. Some invasive plants, such as Japanese knotweed, have had a devastating impact on parts of the UK. Gardeners in the nineteenth century considered it a beautiful ornamental plant - which it is, when it's kept under control - but it soon spread into the countryside and remains a problem even to this day as it's so hard to eradicate. Another invasive plant is rhododendrons, which can be found in UK parks and woodlands. Their introduction dates back to 1763, but they're now seen as harmful because they block out so much light that native wild flowers can't grow beneath them.
sentences.zh: 关于入侵物种的第二个例子来自英国。事实上，英国有三千多种入侵物种，其中一些极为常见。某些入侵植物，例如日本虎杖，已对英国部分地区造成毁灭性影响。十九世纪的园艺爱好者曾视其为一种美丽的观赏植物——确实在受控条件下它确实如此美丽——但它很快蔓延至乡村地区，至今仍难以根除，持续构成难题。另一种入侵植物是杜鹃花属植物（rhododendrons），在英国的公园和林地中随处可见。它们最早于1763年被引入英国，如今却被视为有害物种，因其遮蔽大量阳光，致使本地野花无法在其下方生长。

sentences.text: And then there are grey squirrels, which are one invasive species almost everyone in the UK will have come across. They were brought to the UK from North America and introduced to private estates around the 1870s but are now found everywhere, from forests to city squares. Grey squirrels have outcompeted the smaller, native red squirrels. They both eat the same food, and the grey squirrels carry a type of virus that is deadly to the red squirrels. Red squirrel populations have collapsed, and there are only a handful of sites left in the UK where they're found.
sentences.zh: 此外还有灰松鼠，这是几乎每个英国人都曾见过的一种入侵物种。它们原产于北美，约在1870年代被引入英国，并最初被放养于私人庄园，如今却已遍布各地——从森林到城市广场无处不在。灰松鼠在竞争中压倒了体型更小的本地红松鼠。两者食性相同，且灰松鼠携带一种对红松鼠致命的病毒。红松鼠种群数量急剧下降，目前英国境内仅剩寥寥几处地点尚存其踪迹。

sentences.text: An important question for ecologists worldwide is, what can we do to tackle the problem of invasive species? The first step in controlling invasive species is learning about the behaviour of new species coming into the country. Monitoring is an important part of this, so that we can know if the new species begins to have a negative impact in its new environment. One effective way to keep track of invasive species is to create a database for the whole country. That way, all relevant authorities and agencies can share important information and take whatever action's needed. But the public also have a vital role to play in this process. They should be encouraged to photograph harmful species - because this helps with identification - and then to report when and where these were observed. But it's important to tell people not to destroy or even touch what they've found.
sentences.zh: 对全球生态学家而言，一个关键问题是：我们该如何应对入侵物种问题？控制入侵物种的第一步，是了解新近进入本国的物种的行为特征。监测是这一过程的重要环节，以便我们及时发现该新物种是否开始对其新环境产生负面影响。建立覆盖全国的入侵物种数据库，是追踪此类物种的有效方法。这样，所有相关主管部门与机构便能共享重要信息，并采取必要行动。但公众在此过程中也扮演着至关重要的角色。应鼓励公众拍摄有害物种的照片——这有助于物种识别——然后报告其被观察到的具体时间与地点。但必须提醒公众：切勿破坏或甚至触碰所发现的物种。

sentences.text: Now, I'm going to move on to...
sentences.zh: 接下来，我将转入……
